The same audit block prints GCV 23,202 kJ/kg, volatile matter 41.76 %, fixed carbon 32.15 %, moisture 4.85 %

column15: THE LOWEST OF THE FOUR AS-FIRED PAKISTANI ANALYSES NOW HELD, and for a short while the only one. At 2.38 % it is 47 percent below the booked 4.5 % and sits just below the bottom of that row's own 2.6-10.7 resource range, which is why the band's lo end was moved to admit it. IT WAS BRIEFLY READ AS EVIDENCE THAT THE BOOKED CENTRAL WAS HIGH; the three CDPR/IGC analyses acquired straight afterwards (5.60, 2.75, 5.95) put the booked value inside the observed spread instead. The audit block also prints two mutually inconsistent dates (start 25 June 2012, completion 1 July 2011) - recorded, not silently repaired

column8: Punjab (fixed-chimney kiln; coal from Hyderabad, Sindh)
column11: CDPR/IGC, Table 2 (printed p.17): Hyderabad coal N 1.07, C 58.13, S 2.75, H 5.74 percent; Table 1 moisture 3.69, ash 11.53, VM 30.75 percent, GCV 18.59 MJ/kg. Hyderabad coal costs Rs. 9,000/t against Balochistan's Rs. 14,000/t, which is why the BTK mixes them
column14: WHAT ANY KILN FIRES. The study is explicit that the fixed-chimney kiln burns a two-to-one Hyderabad-Balochistan MIXTURE; this pure sample was collected there but is a component of that charge, not the charge. Also one batch, with no analytical basis printed, and the authors' caution against reading any of these as averages applies
column15: TYPED as_delivered, NOT as_fired, and the distinction changes the sign of the round's conclusion. Counted as a fired fuel it drags the mean of the held analyses to 4.17 percent, just below the booked 4.5, and the evidence reads as mildly supporting a lower central. Excluded, the fired fuels are 2.38, 5.60 and the mixture, the mean is 4.64, and the evidence reads as mildly supporting a HIGHER one. Proportioning this sample into the charge its own kiln burns gives (2 x 2.75 + 5.60)/3 = 3.70 percent, which is what the mixture would assay if it were made of the two pure samples - the study measured 5.95 for a different batch, and that gap is unresolved. Price selects sulfur: Hyderabad coal costs Rs. 9,000/t and assays 2.75, Balochistan costs Rs. 14,000/t and assays 5.60

column11: CDPR/IGC, Table 2 (printed p.17): the mixture N 0.86, C 50.63, S 5.95, H 4.38 percent; Table 1 moisture 10.00, ash 21.00, VM 45.90 percent, GCV 23.13 MJ/kg
column14: the study states the mixture sample came from a DIFFERENT BATCH, and possibly different mines, than the two pure samples - which is why the mixture's sulfur (5.95) exceeds both its components (5.60 and 2.75) instead of lying between them. It is not the proportional sum of the other two rows and must not be read as one
column15: the highest of the four as-fired Pakistani analyses now held

column11: CDPR/IGC Table 5 'Emission Factors and Emission Rates', fuel-mass-based SO2: ZZK 7.97 g/kg, BTK 299.00 g/kg; CO2 2,836 and 8,453 g/kg. Stack sampling used US EPA Methods 2 and 17 with O2, stack velocity, temperature and flow recorded - the terms the Faisalabad campaign omits
column14: RETENTION, although it is the only paired fuel-sulfur and stack-SO2 measurement on Pakistani kilns and ought to determine it. It cannot, because the two kilns give irreconcilable answers
column15: THE FACTORS FAIL ELEMENTAL CONSERVATION AT ONE OF THE TWO KILNS, which is a finding about the document and is why nothing here is booked. Complete conversion of the fuel's own sulfur bounds SO2 at 2 x S: 112 g/kg for the ZZK (5.60 percent S) and 119 for the BTK (5.95). The ZZK's measured 7.97 g/kg is 7 percent of that bound and implies 0.93 retention. The BTK's measured 299.00 g/kg is 2.51 TIMES the bound - impossible from fuel sulfur - and implies a retention of -1.51. The same pattern holds for carbon: the BTK's 8,453 g CO2/kg is 4.55 times what its 50.63 percent carbon can yield, while the ZZK's 2,836 is 1.13 times. The two published factors are internally consistent with each other (EF_e x GCV reproduces EF_m to three figures), so the error is upstream in the BTK's fuel-consumption or stack-flow term, not in the normalisation. CONSEQUENCE: the BTK factors cannot be used, and retention stays unmeasured. The ZZK's 0.93 is a single kiln against a booked 0.25 and rests on a CO2 closure that is itself 13 percent over its own bound

column15: TWO SEARCH-ENGINE READINGS OF THIS PAPER WERE WRONG and are recorded so the error is not repeated: one returned '0.24-0.89 wt %, 10 samples', the other '1.0 % by weight'. The second is the paper's Table 2 PSI LIMIT (1.0 wt % max) mistaken for a measurement. The values above are transcribed from the held PDF. The central above is the mean of the marketer means; the paper's own 0.393 is carried in this note rather than chosen, because the source does not reconcile them
